title: Dynamic quant handoff and latency budgeting manifest (2025 draft)
author: Diego Morales
content:
> **Archived 2026-03-01:** this page is superseded by "Dynamic quant handoff and latency budgeting manifest" and is kept for reference only.

Summary:
This page describes how we operate dynamic quantization handoff: routing requests at runtime between the full-precision model and quantized (or mixed-precision) variants depending on the route's latency budget, KV-cache state, and quality guardrails. It covers safety checks, telemetry, example configuration, and how regressions are triaged across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals and scope:
- Goal: lower per-token cost by sending eligible requests to quantized variants while holding application quality and latency SLOs.
- Scope: text and function-call serving. Multimodal and embedding services need their own calibration.
- Out-of-scope: cross-model reranking, architecture changes, and offline-only quant research.

Key concepts:
- Quant variant: a quantized or mixed-precision build of a base model (fp16 baseline, int8 static, int8+kv-cache hybrid).
- Handoff: the runtime decision to serve a request on a quant variant.
- Latency budget: the p95/p99 SLO target for a route, e.g. p95 <= 150ms for short chat turns.
- Anchored probe: a synthetic input that checks a quant variant keeps a critical response anchor within an allowed delta.

Operational contract:
1) Pre-handoff safety gates (required)
   - Quality sentinel: any active regression on the latest anchor suite disables handoff for that model-version/route.
   - KV-cache compatibility: the quant variant is only eligible when kv-cache-hit-rate >= 50% for the tenant/route (configurable per workload).
   - Token limit: variants built with sequence-length optimized kernels only accept requests <= max_seq_len_quanted.

2) Latency budget enforcement (required)
   - The runtime estimates the expected latency delta from the model profile and the current batching window; if expected_latency_quant > latency_budget the handoff is skipped.
   - Example budgets: interactive-chat (p95 150ms), batch-rerank (p95 400ms).

3) Quality tolerances (required)
   - Per-route coherence delta <= 3.5% on anchored and instruction-following probes, unless a business owner signs off.
   - Function-call endpoints: argument omission rate delta <= 0.5%.

Routing policy matrix (example):
| Route type       | Default latency budget (p95) | KV-cache min hit | Max sequence for quant | Allowed quant tiers |
|------------------|------------------------------|------------------|------------------------|---------------------|
| interactive-chat | 150ms                        | 50%              | 2048                   | int8-hybrid, int8   |
| assistant-long   | 350ms                        | 30%              | 8192                   | mixed16,int8-hybrid |
| rerank-api       | 450ms                        | 0%               | 1024                   | int8                |

Telemetry (minimum):
- quant_handoff_attempts and quant_handoff_success (counts) by route, model_variant, tenant
- quant_expected_latency_delta_ms (gauge)
- anchor_failure_rate by probe_family, variant, route
- coherence_delta_pct over 1h/24h windows
- kv_cache_hit_rate by tenant, route
- cost_per_token_estimate by variant
- rollback_triggers with reasons anchor_regression, latency_violation, downstream_error

Evaluation harness:
- Anchor suite:
  - 200 short-turn instruction probes for the most frequent intents, with golden tokens for token-diff.
  - 50 function-call probes with strict argument assertions.
  - 100 long-context coherence probes over 4-8 turns.
  - 40 adversarial/noise probes for hallucination amplification.

- Offline eval before promotion:
  1. Run the suite on candidate and baseline; collect token-diff, embedding similarity, and function-arg fidelity deltas.
  2. Equivalence test on primary metrics must reach p-value < 0.05, otherwise fail.
  3. Simulate latency with the runtime profiler to estimate expected_latency_delta_ms.
  4. If quality and latency gates pass, open a promotion ticket with the recommended config.

- Shadow validation:
  - 24–48 hour shadow run mirroring 5–20% of traffic for targeted tenants.
  - Track rolling anchor_failure_rate and coherence_delta_pct; if thresholds are exceeded for >30 minutes the canary is revoked automatically.

Rollout playbook:
1) Build and tag the quant candidate (e.g. model-vX-quant-int8-hybrid).
2) Run the offline anchor suite and latency simulation; record results on the promotion ticket.
3) On pass, submit for SHIP review and configure the shadow-mirror experiment (shadow_percentage, probe_injection_rate=5%).
4) Run a 48-hour shadow for low-risk routes; high-risk routes start at 24 hours and escalate.
5) With stable shadow metrics and owner approval, enable handoff for a small tenant subset with strict alerts.
6) Double exposed traffic every 12 hours while watching rollback_triggers.
7) Full enablement: the runtime decides per request.

Failure modes and automated rollback:
- Anchor regression: anchor_failure_rate > threshold (default 1.0%) for 10 consecutive minutes revokes handoffs for that variant/route and opens an incident labeled regression-triage.
- Latency drift: observed p95 more than 20% over latency_budget for 15 minutes drops handoff probability to 0%.
- Downstream errors (503/timeout): downstream_error_rate above 2x baseline within 5 minutes pauses handoffs and pages oncall.

Regression triage:
- Required ticket fields: model_variant, route, tenant_sample, last_good_artifact, anchor_failure_examples (up to 10), token-level and embedding diffs.
- Use the Regression Huntbook (link) hypothesis matrix; prioritize production-impacting regressions.
- Bisect between the quant artifact and last_good_artifact in live replay mode; rank likely causes (kernel mismatch, KV-cache misalignment, tokenizer drift).

Runtime configuration example:
---
route: interactive-chat
policy: dynamic_quant_handoff
allowed_variants: ["int8-hybrid","mixed16"]
min_kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.5
latency_budget_ms_p95: 150
probe_injection_rate: 0.05
handoff_decision: >
  - if kv_cache_hit_rate >= min_kv_cache_hit_rate and expected_latency_delta_ms <= (latency_budget_ms_p95 * 0.2) then enable variant
  - else use baseline
---

Onboarding checklist for model owners:
- [ ] Quant artifact plus profiler file.
- [ ] Anchor suite linked to the promotion ticket.
- [ ] Route-level SLOs and acceptable deltas.
- [ ] Offline suite results attached.
- [ ] Shadow run scheduled and oncall informed.

Ownership and escalation:
- Model owner: Applied ML team for model-vX.
- Runtime owner: Serving-runtime team.
- Oncall: Platform SRE.
- Escalation: Platform SRE -> Applied ML -> Engineering manager -> Head of Inference.

Troubleshooting snippets:
- Force-disable handoff for a tenant:
  redwoodctl routes update --route interactive-chat --set dynamic_quant_handoff.enabled=false --tenant tenant-123
- Latest anchor failures:
  SELECT timestamp, route, tenant, probe_id, diff_type, diff_score FROM telemetry.anchor_failures WHERE model_variant='model-vX-quant-int8-hybrid' ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 50;

Rationale:
- Handoffs favor high KV-cache-hit contexts because quantized kernels can change KV storage and indexing; cached prefixes are more stable.
- Interactive routes reserve 20% of the budget for expected_latency_delta.

Maintenance:
